skill.name: youtube-transcript-extractor-api-skill
skill.description: Extract YouTube transcripts and basic video metadata through the BrowserAct API using a bundled Python helper script.
skill.summary: Runs a BrowserAct workflow to fetch YouTube transcript text and metadata from a video URL.
skill.author: browser-act

security_audit.summary: The skill is an intended BrowserAct API wrapper, not malware, and most Markdown backtick and reconnaissance alerts are false positives. Confirmed risks remain: it sends user URLs and an API key to a third-party API, documents execution of a bundled Python script, and asks users to provide an API key to the agent when missing.

remediation.issue: API key may be disclosed in conversation.
remediation.suggestion: Change the instructions and script output to require setting BROWSERACT_API_KEY locally. Do not ask users to paste the key into chat.

remediation.issue: Target URL is not validated locally.
remediation.suggestion: Validate that TargetURL uses an expected YouTube host before sending it to BrowserAct. Reject unrelated domains with a clear error.

remediation.issue: Community script execution and third-party API calls are required.
remediation.suggestion: Document the exact endpoint, data sent, timeout behavior, and transcript data returned. Require user confirmation before running the script.

semantic_findings.title: API Key Disclosure Request
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells the agent to request the BrowserAct API key when it is missing, and the script says the user may provide it to the agent. This can expose credentials in chat history or logs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Both the usage instructions and runtime message explicitly direct the user toward providing an API key to the agent. The risk is credential exposure outside a local secret store.

semantic_findings.title: Missing YouTube URL Validation
semantic_findings.description: The script accepts a command-line target URL and sends it to the BrowserAct workflow as TargetURL without validating that it is a YouTube domain. If the remote template accepts other URLs, this can enable unintended browsing or data submission.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The local script performs no URL host validation before sending user input to the external API. The remote BrowserAct template may enforce YouTube-only behavior, so confidence is medium.

content.value_statement: Manual transcript copying slows video research. This skill runs BrowserAct's YouTube template to fetch transcript text and metadata from a supplied video URL.
actual_capabilities: Runs a bundled Python script with a supplied YouTube video URL.
Reads the BrowserAct API key from BROWSERACT_API_KEY.
Starts a BrowserAct workflow template for transcript extraction.
Polls task status until the workflow finishes, fails, or times out.
Prints transcript text and video metadata returned by BrowserAct.
limitations: Requires a BrowserAct account and a valid API key.
Sends the target URL and authorization header to BrowserAct.
Does not validate the target URL before sending it to the API.
Depends on YouTube availability, captions, and BrowserAct service status.

use_cases.title: Summarize a Video Lecture
use_cases.description: Extract a transcript from a lecture video so it can be summarized and reviewed quickly.

use_cases.title: Collect Media Research Notes
use_cases.description: Fetch transcript text and publisher metadata for a video used in qualitative research.

use_cases.title: Prepare Content Repurposing
use_cases.description: Convert video speech into text that can support briefs, outlines, and article drafts.

prompt_templates.title: Extract One Transcript
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the YouTube transcript extractor for this video: [URL]. Return the transcript and basic metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize a Video
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract the transcript for [URL], then summarize the main points and note any useful timestamps if available.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Several Videos
prompt_templates.prompt: For these YouTube URLs, extract transcripts one at a time and compare themes, claims, and publisher metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Build Research Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract the transcript and metadata for [URL]. Create research notes with key quotes, claims, and follow-up questions.

output_examples.input: Extract the transcript for a product demo video.
output_examples.output: A transcript with the video title, original link, publisher name, channel link, like count, and spoken text.

output_examples.input: Summarize a webinar after extracting its transcript.
output_examples.output: A concise summary, key takeaways, and notable terms based on the returned transcript.

output_examples.input: Collect metadata for a YouTube interview.
output_examples.output: Publisher details, source video link, engagement metadata, and the full available transcript.

best_practices: Set BROWSERACT_API_KEY locally before running the skill.
Confirm that the URL points to the intended YouTube video.
Review transcript accuracy before using it for important decisions.
anti_patterns: Do not paste API keys into prompts or shared logs.
Do not use the skill for private or unauthorized video content.
Do not assume every video has complete transcript data.

faq.question: Does this skill need an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires BROWSERACT_API_KEY for BrowserAct API access.

faq.question: Does it download the video file?
faq.answer: No. It requests transcript and metadata from a BrowserAct workflow.

faq.question: What data can it return?
faq.answer: It can return transcript text, video title, video URL, publisher, channel link, and like count.

faq.question: Can it process any YouTube video?
faq.answer: Only videos supported by YouTube, BrowserAct, and available transcript data are likely to work.

faq.question: Where is the transcript extracted?
faq.answer: The bundled script sends the target URL to the BrowserAct API and prints the returned result.

faq.question: Is it safe to paste my API key into chat?
faq.answer: No. Set the key as a local environment variable instead.
